book.title: Prophet Noah (pbuh): The Ark and the Flood (A1)

pages.title: Five Great Prophets
pages.content:
Allah sent prophets to people. Five of them were very great prophets. They were very patient and strong in their hearts. They had a very important duty. They showed people the right way to Allah.

These five prophets are Noah (pbuh), Abraham (pbuh), Moses (pbuh), Jesus (pbuh) and Muhammad (pbuh). This is the story of Prophet Noah (pbuh).

vocabulary.definition: Make someone go to a place.
A person who brings Allah's words to people.
Can wait a long time and not get angry.

hotspots.title: Prophets
hotspots.description: Allah sent prophets to people. They showed people the right way to Allah.

hotspots.title: Five Great Prophets
hotspots.description: These five prophets are Noah (pbuh), Abraham (pbuh), Moses (pbuh), Jesus (pbuh) and Muhammad (pbuh).

exercises.title: Five Great Prophets
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 1?

items: The five prophets were very patient.
They showed people the right way to Allah.
Noah (pbuh) is not one of the five great prophets.

True: The five prophets were very patient.
They showed people the right way to Allah.
False: Noah (pbuh) is not one of the five great prophets.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says: “They were very patient and strong in their hearts.” “They showed people the right way to Allah.” “These five prophets are Noah (pbuh), Abraham (pbuh), Moses (pbuh), Jesus (pbuh) and Muhammad (pbuh).”

feedback.correct: Yes! Noah (pbuh) is one of the five.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Patient
languageFocusExercises.question: “They were very patient.” What does a patient person do?
options: waits a long time and does not get angry
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Patient = can wait a long time and not get angry.

feedback.correct: Yes. A patient person waits and is calm.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 1 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Was, Were
languageFocusExercises.question: One or many?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: They (many) → were. This (one) → was.

feedback.incorrect: They = many. This = one.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Patient People
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Talk about patience with your partner.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who is patient?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use is patient.

discussionPrompts.question: “I am patient when …”
discussionPrompts.example: I am patient when I wait for the bus.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: How many very great prophets are there?
beforeYouRead.quote: Five of them were very great prophets.

iCan: I can tell about the five great prophets.
I can understand patient.
I can talk about patient people.

pages.title: Good Men and Stone Statues
pages.content:
After Prophet Adam (pbuh), many people lived on the earth. At first, they worshipped only Allah. They remembered the prophets’ words and prayed only to Allah. Later, people forgot Allah’s words. But there were five good men. They still prayed to Allah day and night. People loved them very much. Their names were Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya’uq and Nasr.

When these good men died, the people missed them. First, they made their pictures. Later, they made statues of them. After many years, people forgot Allah and started to pray to statues of these five men. This was very wrong.

vocabulary.definition: Feel sad because a person is not with you.
A big figure of a person, made of stone.

hotspots.title: Five Good Men
hotspots.description: Five good men still prayed to Allah day and night. People loved them very much.

hotspots.title: Statues
hotspots.description: After many years, people forgot Allah and started to pray to statues of these five men.

exercises.title: Good Men and Stone Statues
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: The people made pictures of them.
The people made statues of them.
The people started to pray to the statues.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: the men died → pictures → statues → people prayed to the statues.

feedback.correct: Great! You put the chapter in order.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: First, Later
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each sentence in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: When was it?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: First → later → after many years: these words tell the order.

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Missed, Forgot, Made
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form tells the past?

formChoices.sentence: When these good men died, the people [choice] them.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Miss → missed: it adds -ed. Forget → forgot, make → made: they change.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 2 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write It: I Miss …
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write about a person you miss.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who do you miss?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use I miss.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did the people make?
beforeYouRead.quote: Later, they made statues of them.

iCan: I can tell how people started to pray to statues.
I can use first and later.
I can write about a person I miss.

pages.title: Noah’s Message
pages.content:
Then Allah sent Noah (pbuh) to these people. Noah was kind, honest and patient. He always said true words. He said to his people, “O my people, worship Allah. You have no god but Him.” (Surah al-A‘râf, 59) He also told them, “I am a Messenger of Allah. Do not pray to statues.”

Some people listened to him and believed him. Most of them were poor and weak. For Allah, poor people and rich people are the same.

vocabulary.definition: A person who brings words from Allah.

hotspots.title: A Messenger
hotspots.description: Noah said, “I am a Messenger of Allah. Do not pray to statues.”

hotspots.title: The Believers
hotspots.description: Some people listened to him and believed him. Most of them were poor and weak.

exercises.title: Noah’s Message
exercises.question: Who believed Noah (pbuh) first?
options: some people, most of them poor and weak
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “Some people listened to him and believed him. Most of them were poor and weak.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Most of them were poor and weak.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Opposites
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match the word with its opposite.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the opposite?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “For Allah, poor people and rich people are the same.” Weak = not strong.

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Said, Told, Believed
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form tells the past?

formChoices.sentence: He also [choice] them, “I am a Messenger of Allah.”

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Say → said, tell → told: they change. Believe → believed: it adds -d.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 3 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: A Good Friend
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner about a good friend.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is your friend like?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use is + kind / honest / patient and always.

discussionPrompts.question: “My friend is kind and …”
discussionPrompts.example: My friend is kind and honest.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What was Noah (pbuh) like?
beforeYouRead.quote: Noah was kind, honest and patient.

iCan: I can tell about Noah’s message.
I can use opposites: rich – poor, weak – strong.
I can talk about a good friend.

pages.title: The Rich Men Say No
pages.content:
The rich and important men did not listen to Noah. They were proud. They said: “You are only a man like us.” (Surah Hûd, 27)

Noah answered, “Yes, I am a man, and I am a Messenger of Allah.” Then the rich men said, “Tell the poor people to go. Then we can come to you.” But Noah said that the believers would stay with him.

vocabulary.definition: Big and strong in a group; people listen to them.
Thinking that you are better than others.
A person who believes in Allah.

hotspots.title: Proud Men
hotspots.description: The rich and important men did not listen to Noah. They were proud.

hotspots.title: The Believers Stay
hotspots.description: Noah said that the believers would stay with him.

exercises.title: The Rich Men Say No
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 4?

items: The rich men said, “Tell the poor people to go.”

True: The rich men said, “Tell the poor people to go.”

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says: “They were proud.” “Then the rich men said, ‘Tell the poor people to go.’” “But Noah said that the believers would stay with him.”

feedback.correct: Yes! The believers stayed with him.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Like Us
languageFocusExercises.question: “You are only a man like us.” What did the rich men mean?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Like us = the same as us.

feedback.correct: Yes. They said he was the same as them.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Did Not
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words go in the gap?

formChoices.sentence: The rich men [choice] listen to Noah.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Past negative: did not + verb. The rich men did not listen.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 4 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Like Me
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner who is like you.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who is like you?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use like + person.

discussionPrompts.question: “My brother is like me. We …”
discussionPrompts.example: My brother is like me. We love football.

discussionPrompts.question: “For Allah, all people are …”
discussionPrompts.example: For Allah, all people are the same.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Did the rich men listen to Noah (pbuh)?
beforeYouRead.quote: The rich and important men did not listen to Noah.

iCan: I can tell what the rich men said.
I can understand like us.
I can use did not.

pages.title: Nine Hundred and Fifty Years
pages.content:
Noah talked to his people day and night for 950 years. He did not want money from them. He only wanted to show the right way.

But the people did not change. When Noah talked, they put their fingers in their ears and laughed at him. Later, they became cruel and hurt him. But Noah stayed patient. In the end, Allah told Noah, “Nobody from your people will believe.” (Surah Hûd, 36) Noah prayed to Allah, “My Lord, do not leave any bad people on the earth. They lead good people to the wrong way.” (Surah Nûh, 26–27) Allah accepted his prayer.

vocabulary.definition: Very bad and unkind to others.

hotspots.title: Day and Night
hotspots.description: Noah talked to his people day and night for 950 years. He did not want money from them.

hotspots.title: Patient
hotspots.description: The people laughed at him and hurt him. But Noah stayed patient.

exercises.title: Nine Hundred and Fifty Years
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Noah talked to his people for 950 years.
The people became cruel and hurt him.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: 950 years → they laughed → they became cruel → Allah accepted his prayer.

feedback.correct: Great! You put the chapter in order.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: For + Time
languageFocusExercises.question: “Noah talked to his people day and night for 950 years.” What does “for 950 years” tell us?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: For + time tells how long: for 950 years, for two hours.

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Noah Stayed Patient
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: He did [blank] want money from them. The people [blank] at him. [blank] Noah stayed patient.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Did not + verb. Laugh → laughed. But shows a different idea.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 5 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write It: Be Patient
languageFocusExercises.question: When are you patient?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use for + time and because.

discussionPrompts.question: “I wait for … for … minutes.”
discussionPrompts.example: I wait for the bus for ten minutes.

discussionPrompts.question: “I am patient because …”
discussionPrompts.example: I am patient because it is good.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: How long did Noah (pbuh) talk to his people?
beforeYouRead.quote: Noah talked to his people day and night for 950 years.

iCan: I can tell how Noah (pbuh) stayed patient.
I can use for + time.
I can write about being patient.

pages.title: A Ship on the Land
pages.content:
Allah told Noah to build an ark. So Noah and the believers started to build a very big ship. They used wood and nails, and they built it far from the sea.

People walked past and laughed at Noah. “Look! A ship, but there is no sea here!” they said. But Noah kept working, because he trusted Allah. Then the ark was ready.

vocabulary.definition: Make a house, a ship or a building.
A small, thin piece of metal for wood.
Believe that someone is good and true.
Finished; you can use it now.

hotspots.title: Wood and Nails
hotspots.description: They used wood and nails, and they built it far from the sea.

hotspots.title: People Laughed
hotspots.description: “Look! A ship, but there is no sea here!” they said.

exercises.title: A Ship on the Land
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 6?

items: They built the ark far from the sea.
They built the ark with stones.

True: They built the ark far from the sea.
False: They built the ark with stones.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “They used wood and nails, and they built it far from the sea.” “But Noah kept working, because he trusted Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes! They used wood and nails.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Because
languageFocusExercises.question: “But Noah kept working, because he trusted Allah.” Why did Noah (pbuh) keep working?
options: He was afraid of the people.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Because tells why: because he trusted Allah.

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: There Is, There Is No
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words go in the gap?

formChoices.sentence: [choice] a very big ship on the land.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: There is a … = one thing is here. There is no … = it is not here.

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: I Made It
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Tell your partner about a thing you made.
languageFocusExercises.question: What did you make?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use made and used.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Noah (pbuh) and the believers build?
beforeYouRead.quote: So Noah and the believers started to build a very big ship.

iCan: I can tell about the ark.
I can use because.
I can say there is no ….

groupTask.title: Building the Ark
steps: The group draws the ark on the land, far from the sea.
The group writes the things they used: wood and nails.
One student writes what the people said. One student writes why Noah kept working.
The group shows the poster to the class.
groupTask.share: One student reads the poster. Story: “But Noah kept working, because he trusted Allah.”
groupTask.solo: Draw the ark. Write two sentences from the chapter.

pages.title: The Great Flood
pages.content:
Then heavy rain came down from the sky. Water came up from the ground, too. This was the flood. Allah told Noah to go into the ark. The believers and two of every animal went in with him.

Noah’s wife and one of his sons did not believe. Noah saw his son near the ship and called, “My son, come with us!” His son said, “I will go up a mountain. It will keep me safe from the water.” Noah said, “Today, nobody is safe from Allah’s order. Only the people with His mercy are safe.” (Surah Hûd, 42–43) Then a big wave came between them, and the son drowned.

vocabulary.definition: Stop bad things from happening to someone.
A big moving line of water in the sea.

hotspots.title: The Flood
hotspots.description: Heavy rain came down from the sky. Water came up from the ground, too.

hotspots.title: Two of Every Animal

languageFocusExercises.question: “I will go up a mountain.” When is this?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Came, Went, Saw
languageFocusExercises.question: Which form tells the past?

formChoices.sentence: Then heavy rain [choice] down from the sky.
Noah [choice] his son near the ship.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Come → came, go → went, see → saw in the past.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 7 again.

languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say animals in pairs with your partner.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which animals went into the ark?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use two + animals and will.

pages.title: A New Start
pages.content:
Then Allah said: “O earth, take back your water! O sky, stop!” (Surah Hûd, 44) The water went down, and the ark stopped on Mount Judi.

Noah opened the door. The animals and birds went out and lived all over the earth. Noah and the believers came out, too. Noah put his head on the ground and thanked Allah.

Many years later, Noah was very old. He gave advice to his children. He told them to believe only in Allah and never to be proud.

vocabulary.definition: Words that help someone do the right thing.

hotspots.description: The animals and birds went out and lived all over the earth.

exercises.title: A New Start
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 8?

items: The animals lived all over the earth.
Noah (pbuh) told his children to be proud.

True: The animals lived all over the earth.
False: Noah (pbuh) told his children to be proud.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 8 says: “Noah put his head on the ground and thanked Allah.” “He told them to believe only in Allah and never to be proud.”

feedback.correct: Yes! He told them never to be proud.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 8 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Told Them to …
languageFocusExercises.question: “He told them to believe only in Allah and never to be proud.” What did Noah (pbuh) say?
options: “Believe only in Allah. Never be proud.”
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Told + person + to + verb: He told them to believe. Never to be = do not be.

feedback.incorrect: Read the last paragraph of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: A New Start
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
languageFocusExercises.question: What happened?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: The water went [blank], and the ark stopped on Mount Judi. Noah [blank] the door. He put his head on the ground and [blank] Allah.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Went down ≠ went up. Open → opened, thank → thanked.

feedback.incorrect: Read the first two paragraphs of Chapter 8.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write It: Good Advice
languageFocusExercises.question: What is good advice?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use always and never + verb.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Where did the ark stop?
beforeYouRead.quote: The water went down, and the ark stopped on Mount Judi.

iCan: I can tell about the new start.
I can understand told them to ….
I can write good advice.

groupTask.title: Noah’s Advice Poster
steps: The group writes Noah’s advice in the middle of the poster.
Each student writes one more piece of good advice: “Always …” or “Never …”.
The group draws the ark on Mount Judi.
The group reads the advice to the class.
groupTask.share: The group reads the poster. Story: “He gave advice to his children.”
groupTask.solo: Write Noah’s advice and two more pieces of advice.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: pray → prayed, miss → missed. Some verbs change: send → sent, forget → forgot, build → built, come → came.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: pray, send … Does it add -ed or change?

feedback.incorrect: Find these words in Chapters 5, 7 and 8.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Choose the right word.
exercises.question: Which word is wrong?

errorItems.sentence: Noah and the believers builded a ship.

exercises.explanation: “Build” and “forget” change in the past: built, forgot.

feedback.incorrect: Build → built. Forget → forgot. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: Patience
exercises.question: When are you patient?
exercises.explanation: Use patient, because and never.

discussionPrompts.question: One “patient”: “I am patient when …”
discussionPrompts.example: I am patient when I help my brother.

discussionPrompts.question: One “because”: “… because …”
discussionPrompts.example: I wait because my friend is late.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole story together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: Five Great Prophets
exercises.question: What were the five prophets like?
exercises.fillBlanksText: They were very [blank] and strong in their hearts.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “They were very patient and strong in their hearts.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Five Good Men
exercises.question: What did people do after the five good men died?
options: They made their pictures and then statues.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “First, they made their pictures. Later, they made statues of them.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Poor and Rich
exercises.question: For Allah, poor people and rich people are the same.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “For Allah, poor people and rich people are the same.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Who Said It?
exercises.instructions: Match the people with their words.
exercises.question: Who said it?

matchingPairs.right: “Look! A ship, but there is no sea here!”

correctAnswer.the people: “Look! A ship, but there is no sea here!”

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: the rich men. Chapter 6: the people. Chapter 7: Noah’s son.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 4, 6 and 7 again.

exercises.title: The People
exercises.question: What did the people do when Noah (pbuh) talked?
options: They put their fingers in their ears.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “When Noah talked, they put their fingers in their ears and laughed at him.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: The Ark
exercises.question: They built the ark near the sea.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: “They used wood and nails, and they built it far from the sea.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is false. It was far from the sea.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: The Flood
exercises.question: Where did the water come from?
options: from the sky and from the ground
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Then heavy rain came down from the sky. Water came up from the ground, too.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Story of Noah (pbuh)
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Allah sent Noah (pbuh) to the people.
Noah (pbuh) and the believers built the ark.
The ark stopped on Mount Judi.

exercises.explanation: Noah’s message (Chapter 3) → the ark (Chapter 6) → the flood (Chapter 7) → Mount Judi (Chapter 8).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of Noah (pbuh).
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
